jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: Grace Period
jokes.joke: My six-year-old insisted on saying grace at dinner. He closed his eyes and said, “Dear God, thank you for Mommy, thank you for me, and please give Daddy the strength to finish his vegetables… because we’re not buying another shovel.”

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: The Bends
jokes.joke: I dated a deep sea diver for three months. Incredible guy, terrible communicator, because his whole personality was formed at depths where sound doesn't carry and neither does emotional nuance. I'd say 'we need to talk,' and he'd just stare at me like I was a fish that wandered too close to a vent. Breaking up with him was cruel, but also efficient, because he genuinely thought silence meant things were fine at any pressure.

jokes.title: Depth Check
jokes.joke: My new girlfriend told me she’s 'very spiritual' and wanted us to connect on a deeper level. I took that literally. Next thing she knows, I’ve got her strapped into a nine-hundred-pound pressurized diving suit dropping off the back of a tugboat. At two hundred feet down in pitch-black water, I radioed through her helmet: 'Feel the energy?'

jokes.title: Even the Fish Have Standards
jokes.joke: I took up deep-sea diving for some peace and quiet. First time I hit the bottom it got spiritual real fast. I started confessing my whole life to a lanternfish. The fish just stared, blinked once, and swam away. Turns out even the deep sea has standards.

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Career Day Depths
jokes.joke: I did career day at an elementary school because I used to work as a deep-sea diver. I told the kids, "The ocean is so dark down there, your flashlight only shows a few feet." One creepy little kid raised his hand and asked, "So how do you know something isn't following you the rest of the way?" I was there to inspire children, and this kid gave me a brand-new fear.

scores.comment: Clear premise, but the pressure metaphors sprawl and the final line explains rather than lands.
The literal deeper-level turn is predictable, and the elaborate diving setup produces only a mild tag.
Clean and economical, but the judgmental-animal ending is familiar and only mildly amusing.
The child's question creates a vivid, relatable chill; the closing line is clear but not a strong final escalation.
Clean, well-timed kid joke with a solid final line; slightly familiar dark-humor-kid template but executed well.
Strong literalized-metaphor premise with good escalation and a snappy closing line that lands the turn.
Decent premise and clean form, but the punchline is soft and restates the idea more than snaps it.
Fresh angle on 'creepy kid,' natural stage voice, and a punchline that genuinely subverts the career-day setup.
Solid escalation and crisp punchline timing, though the 'kid secretly planning a murder' premise is a familiar trope.
More of an essayistic observation than a stage joke; it explains its metaphors thoroughly rather than snapping on a strong punchline.
Competent structure and easy to follow, but the 'even X rejected me' ending is a well-worn stand-up formula.
Good stage rhythm and relatable reaction, though stating 'creepy little kid' in the setup slightly front-runs the punchline.
Tight prayer setup with a dark shovel turn; the kid's threat lands as shock more than pure laugh for a broad room.
Clear concept but wordy explanation dilutes the payoff; ends more as observation than a snap.
Strong literal escalation from spiritual to diving suit; the radio line is clean but the premise stays a bit mean.
Solid career-day premise with a creepy-kid question that cleanly flips the inspirational talk into fear.
Strong creepy turn from an innocent prayer setup. Clear escalation and a memorable final image.
Consistent relationship analogy but somewhat stretched. More clever observation than punch-driven joke.
Solid literal misunderstanding premise with a vivid image. Payoff is amusing but not especially sharp.
Clean stand-up structure and readable rhythm. 'Even the deep sea has standards' is familiar in shape but works.
